assembly_notes: Small hand-driven demonstration generator. The grounded `frame` part carries two parallel +y shaft lines on open saddle bearings: the input line at -centre_distance/2 and the armature line at +centre_distance/2. The `input` part turns CONTINUOUS on the first and the `rotor` part turns CONTINUOUS on the second, mimic-coupled at the ratio of the two wheel radii, which are themselves derived from the shaft centre distance. drive_input varies the hand end: an offset crank web with a grip spinning on its own pin, two opposed cranks and grips, a spoked handwheel on the axis itself, or a rimmed flywheel beside the crank. transmission varies what couples the two lines: a jackshaft and flat pulley train, a meshed spur pair, a flat belt over two pulleys, that belt with a sprung idler on its own CONTINUOUS joint, rubber friction wheels with a PRISMATIC tension carrier, or a right-angle bevel transfer shaft. stator_form varies the electrical hardware around the armature: plain pole pieces, a slotted U-bridge, twin magnet posts, or a bolted gearbox side plate with a pole ring; each also lays out the coil packs on the armature and the terminal posts on the base. All rotating members are bodies of revolution about their own axis apart from the crank web and grip, which are placed outboard of the frame so their swept circle stays in free air. shaft_height_m, centre_distance_m and rotor_radius_m are the honest continuous parameters; coil_count and terminal_count are the multiplicities; palette is neither.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: 1 <= coil_count <= 3; the pack width is derived from the coil pitch so adjacent packs keep a real gap at the smallest armature radius
multiplicities.name: coil_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: coil pack k sits at 2*pi*k/coil_count around the armature axis

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: 2 <= terminal_count <= 4; the cap diameter is derived from the terminal pitch so adjacent posts never touch
multiplicities.name: terminal_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: terminal k sits at k * terminal_pitch_m along the derived base pad
